title: dollhouse as micro-worlds, pisces I
content:
this series is created for my collaboration with LJ of Ceremony for their communal writing practice, Atmospheres, based on the 36 decans of the astrological year.

Pisces I, Dollhouse — February 18-28
Key themes from LJ — tiny artifacts, dreamscapes, hidden moons
Before this: Aquarius III, exploding other worlds


this decan is about the dollhouse minature as microcosm — using a diorama model to reveal something hidden about the nature of reality. it reminds me of playing house as a child — what could we enact as theatre, except what we saw in our daily lives — and, in the stories and media we consumed? this feels like the same exercise in reverse. how would our lives look differently if we were to put it in minature form, or to create smaller vessels to hold it? what would we learn about ourselves?

there is something about the dollhouse that fills me with a domestic dread — until I realize that I can put whatever I want inside of it. it is a house of my imagination, not unlike a website. (is a website a digital dollhouse? a micro-cosm? I actually think of it as something more expansive, representing consciousness; a universe of its own) there is also something about the dollhouse that feels like playing god, exerting dominion and control.

could we make dollhouse minatures to give parts of our psyche room to play, experiment, and roam? when faced with a difficult life decisions, could we run imaginative simulations in which we put versions of ourselves in those dollhouse worlds, set a timer for compressed time, just to see what would happen? the dollhouse is creating the environmental conditions, but it’s also missing an element of chance, circumstance, the wild ride that is the wheel of fortune. still, I find this exercise potentially meaningful and enlightening.

~

I was inspired by the shades of green I remember seeing in Guillermo del Toro’s Frankenstein (2025). they’ve been lingering in the back of my mind, and perhaps one day I’ll write about it. (Frankenstein is also a story of miniatures, of the doctor playing God).
